analytical_question: How far have generative-AI ambient scribes and primary-care note drafting diffused, what drives or inhibits spread, and what pilot timing follows for this organization?
general_et_finding: Published U.S. health-system examples show ambient scribing moving beyond isolated experiments into large deployments, but the supplied evidence has no representative national denominator or comparable time series for ambient-scribe use. The U.S. market adopter category is therefore indeterminate; the cited health systems are examples of pioneering/early-adopter organizations, not proof that the market has reached the early majority. The AMA 2026 81% figure concerns any physician AI awareness/use, not ambient scribing.
application_finding: Outpatient primary-care note drafting is demonstrated in multi-specialty ambulatory settings, but no supplied source estimates its U.S. primary-care or safety-net peer prevalence. Rogers factors — Relative advantage: a 66-clinician randomized implementation found 0.36 fewer note-writing hours/day, but local savings are unmeasured. Compatibility: EHR-connected workflows help; device requirements, consent, languages and note templates may hinder local fit. Complexity: setup, clinician editing and training remain work. Trialability: a small opt-in pilot can test workflow without committing to system-wide rollout. Observability: note-use share, time, corrections and clinician/patient feedback can be monitored, though actual local baselines are absent. Vanderbilt clinician champions and training promoted uptake; integration and privacy/safety validation are complementary assets and potential inhibitors. These are mechanisms or plausible transfers, not a measured local diffusion rate.

evidence.claim: In the 2026 physician survey, 81% reported any AI awareness/use; 88% rated trusted safety/efficacy validation and 86% privacy assurances important.
evidence.date_or_recency: Survey Jan 15-Feb 2, 2026; report Mar 2026; checked Oct 24, 2026
evidence.evidence_type: Original voluntary U.S. physician self-report survey; 1,692 participants, item denominators vary
evidence.notes: Broad AI and expressed prerequisites; not ambient-scribe use, representative prevalence, or demonstrated effectiveness.

evidence.claim: After Vanderbilt made an EHR-integrated ambient scribe available to over 2,400 ambulatory/ED clinicians, 1,223 had used it and 20.1% of all visit notes involved it by Mar 31, 2025; leaders/champions and low-barrier training supported rollout.
evidence.notes: Ever-use and note-share differ; ambulatory plus ED; not a national or safety-net denominator. No causal attribution of adoption to champions.

evidence.claim: In a randomized implementation with 66 volunteer ambulatory clinicians, 27,092 of 71,487 notes (38%) used ambient AI and note-writing time fell by 0.36 h/day.
evidence.date_or_recency: Study Aug 2024-Mar 2025; NEJM AI Nov 26, 2025; checked Oct 24, 2026
evidence.evidence_type: Original single-system pragmatic randomized trial; eight specialties
evidence.notes: Trial estimates benefit/feasibility among eligible volunteers; 38% is within-trial note share, not market penetration or primary-care prevalence.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: No representative U.S. ambient-scribe or comparable primary-care peer adoption series is supplied; Rogers market stage cannot be assigned confidently.
The AMA self-report instrument covers AI broadly and changed across waves; it cannot establish ambient-scribe prevalence.
Single-system implementation and volunteer trial may not transfer to resource-limited, multilingual safety-net care; local effect, cost and error rates are unknown.
organization_specific_finding: This fast-following network has basic integration and analytic capacity but limited training and no multilingual validation. It can prepare a pilot sooner than the conservative network, yet should wait for a relevant peer signal and finish local checks. The same external evidence remains unchanged.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate-low confidence in a 3-6 month pilot window because peer data and language validation are missing; low confidence in national market stage. Organization details are hypothetical.
value_opportunity_implication: A bounded pilot could test local note-time savings and fit; published time savings are a hypothesis for this network.
risk_governance_implication: Require privacy and consent workflow, clinician sign-off, training, note-correction tracking and language-specific validation.
recommendation_management_implication: Prepare now and consider a limited opt-in pilot in about 3-6 months if a comparable primary-care peer report, local integration and privacy review, and multilingual checks are satisfactory; this is not a purchase or rollout verdict.
change_monitoring_triggers: Comparable primary-care peer report gives actual active-use and note-share denominators.
Local EHR/consent/privacy and multilingual tests pass.
Training capacity and note-quality monitoring are funded.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Abstain from a national diffusion-stage label.
Do not set a live pilot date until peer and local checks meet preset criteria.
